report:
Uterus with cervix and bilateral adnexa, total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; peritoneal tumour debulking

The specimen consists of an intact uterus with cervix and bilateral adnexa from a total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy. The ovaries and fallopian tubes are grossly unremarkable; the peritoneal tumour measures 30 mm in greatest dimension. The outer surface is smooth. The fallopian tube is unremarkable. The uterus with cervix (70 x 45 x 30 mm) and both adnexa are grossly unremarkable; the rectovaginal peritoneum bears a 30 mm tumour nodule.

(1) Cervix.
(2-3) Endometrium and myometrium.
(4-5) Right adnexa, tube entirely embedded.
(6-7) Left adnexa, tube entirely embedded.
(8-11) Peritoneal tumour.

Specimen and tumour
- Procedure: Total hysterectomy and bilateral salpingo-oophorectomy; peritoneal
  tumour debulking
- Hysterectomy type: Abdominal
- Specimen integrity (right ovary): Capsule intact
- Specimen integrity (left ovary): Capsule intact
- Specimen integrity (right fallopian tube): Serosa intact
- Specimen integrity (left fallopian tube): Serosa intact
- Tumour site: Primary peritoneum
- Ovarian surface involvement: Not identified
- Fallopian tube surface involvement: Not identified
- Tumour size: 30 mm in greatest dimension

Microscopic findings
- Histologic type: High-grade serous carcinoma
- Histologic grade: Not applicable (high grade by definition)
- Tumour histology:
  Sections show a high-grade serous carcinoma. The tumour grows in solid sheets
  punctuated by slit-like spaces, with hierarchical papillary branching and
  cribriform and glandular areas. The cells are cuboidal to columnar with
  eosinophilic cytoplasm and markedly pleomorphic, hyperchromatic nuclei
  including bizarre and multinucleated forms, with large eosinophilic nucleoli.
  Mitotic figures are numerous and include atypical forms, geographic and
  comedo-type necrosis is present, and tumour-infiltrating lymphocytes and
  psammoma bodies are seen. The fallopian tubes are examined entirely (SEE-FIM)
  and the mucosa is not involved. Immunohistochemistry: p53 shows an abnormal
  pattern (strong diffuse nuclear overexpression); WT1 positive, PAX8 positive,
  ER positive.
- Lymphovascular invasion: Present
- p53 immunohistochemistry: Abnormal, Overexpression (strong, diffuse nuclear
  expression, more than 90%)
- Largest extrapelvic peritoneal focus: Not applicable
- Peritoneal / ascitic fluid: Malignant cells present
- Other tissue / organ involvement: Pelvic peritoneum; Rectal wall

Margins
- Ectocervical / vaginal cuff margin: Uninvolved by carcinoma
- Parametrial / paracervical margin: Not applicable

Lymph nodes
- Regional lymph nodes: Not submitted

Distant metastasis
- Distant metastasis: Not identified

Pathological stage (AJCC 8th edition)
- pTNM: pT2b pNX
  - Stage group (if cM0): IIB

Additional findings
- None

UTERUS WITH CERVIX AND BILATERAL ADNEXA, total hysterectomy and bilateral
salpingo-oophorectomy
- HIGH-GRADE SEROUS CARCINOMA, primary peritoneal, 30 mm; see synoptic report
- involving the pelvic peritoneum and rectal wall; peritoneal fluid positive for
  malignant cells; lymphovascular invasion present
- pT2b pNX (AJCC 8th edition), stage IIB (if cM0)

checks.message: Primary peritoneal carcinoma: stage cannot be I; the ovaries and tubes must be grossly normal and microscopically free or minimally involved (WHO 5th).
Positive peritoneal fluid is recorded; it only sets the stage (pT1c3 / IC3) when the tumour is confined to the ovaries or tubes.
FIGO 2014 (reference, not reported; FIGO Cancer Report 2025 reproduces the 2014 table): IIB
